cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

mechanism: A claims control of household timing while repeatedly handing B a forced choice when B practical solutions create new simultaneous duties.
confusable: Unlike simple inability to multitask, A demands B choose both urgent obligations; confident control must incorporate B solution without letting the choice game end.
comparison: Dinner stirring and suitcase help differ from a collecting route and a live call during a depot deadline.
seedUse: Use D34-a gravy/taxi/suitcase progression with S02-a treating B new arrangement as the plan while preserving cooperation.
